title: Ratiometric Single-Molecule FRET Measurements to Probe Conformational Subpopulations of Intrinsically Disordered Proteins
protocol: Measure the distance between two fluorophores using smFRET.
Collect donor and acceptor bursts simultaneously for smFRET experiments.
Filter bursts originating from the same molecules for data analysis.
Calculate FRET efficiency values from collected data.
Approximate FRET efficiency by a Gaussian distribution ranging from 0 to 1.
Fit the curve with a Gaussian function for an average FRET efficiency value.
Solve an integral for an appropriate probability density function for distance distributions.
Switch the laser power on and allow it to stabilize for at least 15 min.
Monitor the laser power and fluctuations until the power has stabilized.
Adjust the laser power to a desired value (100-150 µW).
Remove the laser power meter from the beam path.
Place a drop of water or oil on the objective with a dropper.
Place and align an appropriate surface at the sample plane to reflect excitation light back through the objective.
Turn off the APDs before proceeding with alignment steps.
Adjust the pinhole to be as large as possible.
Remove spectral filters and dichroic mirrors from the beam path, but keep lenses and other beam-shaping optics in place.
Use a mirror to check if the beam falls within the detector surface of the APD that detects light transmitted through the first dichroic mirror.
Change the APD position until the beam is centered within the APD face.
Replace the first dichroic mirror.
Check that the reflected beam falls in the middle of any reflective mirrors using a white card or piece of paper.
Adjust the position of the reflected beam toward the APD face if necessary.
Adjust the dichroic mirror to reflect the beam roughly in the middle of the APD detector opening.
Adjust the second APD as described in step 8.
Proceed to adjust additional APDs as needed, starting from the least reflection-dependent APD.
Place all filters back in the beam path after the objective.
Insert a pinhole of desired diameter into the light path.
Replace reflective surface with a sample chamber filled with free donor fluorophore at low nanomolar concentration.
Start with lower laser power (20 μW).
Increase laser power to desired value as needed.
Decrease frequency of data collection as necessary for signal of ∼10-50 kHz.
Turn on the APDs and data acquisition program.
Adjust pinhole position until signal from the APDs is maximized.
Reduce laser power if needed during alignment.
Go back to large/no pinhole setup (step 6) if required.
Adjust APD positions to maximize signal.
Return to step 12 after adjusting APD positions.
Individually adjust APDs further to maximize the signal.
Turn off the ADPs after no further improvements are recorded.
Adjust the objective to focus the beam in the sample.
Dilute the α-synuclein (or other protein) sample with sterile-filtered protein dilution buffer.
Add suitable photoprotectors to the diluted sample.
Ensure the final concentration of dual-labeled protein is ∼100 pM.
Add 200 μl of the solution to the coverslip chamber.
Let the solution sit for 5 min before measurement.
Turn on the APDs and data acquisition program.
Adjust the acquisition frequency in the data acquisition program.
Insert direct excitation, leakage, and signal threshold values if using a real-time data visualization program.
Run the experiment.
Once the experiment is complete, turn off APDs and laser.
Remove the sample chamber.
Wipe off the objective with objective cleaning wipes.
Process binned photon counts.
Calculate FRET efficiency.
Subtract the contributions of background from the raw donor and acceptor photon streams for ratiometric smFRET measurements.
At low single-molecule concentrations, obtain an estimate of background intensity by averaging all photon counts within one channel over the course of data acquisition time.
Process background-corrected photon streams to obtain intensities corrected for leakage and direct excitation.
Use the procedure in Support Protocol 3 to obtain corrected donor and acceptor intensities.

Apply a threshold (“T”) to the sum of donor and acceptor intensities within the same time bin (SUM = ID + IA > T) to identify qualifying bursts of donor and acceptor that originate from the same single molecule.
Reject donor and acceptor bursts that sum to less than “T” in the case of SUM criteria.
Label Cys residues of the protein of interest via maleimide chemistry using maleimide-conjugated Alexa Fluor 488 (donor) and Alexa Fluor 594 (acceptor).
Prepare fluorophore solutions in an organic solvent such as dimethyl formamide (DMF) or dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO).
Incubate the protein of interest with a reducing agent like dithiothreitol (DTT) or tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine (TCEP).
Exchange buffer using a NAP column or HiTrap desalting column.
Remove excess fluorophores and unreacted reagents using a centrifugal filter device or dialysis device.
Dissolve 1 mg of each fluorophore in 200 µl of the organic solvent suggested by the manufacturer.
Measure the stock concentrations by UV-visible (UV-Vis) spectrometry.
Prepare 10-µl aliquots and store up to 6 months at −80°C.
Alternatively, evaporate the organic solvent using a vacuum centrifuge concentrator.
Prepare labeling buffer consisting of 20 mM Tris•Cl and 150 mM NaCl, pH 7.5.
Sterilize the labeling buffer by passing it through a 0.2-μm filter.
Dissolve α-synuclein (or other protein of interest) in the labeling buffer if lyophilized.
Buffer exchange the protein into the labeling buffer using gel filtration or a centrifugal filter device if already dissolved in another buffer.
Concentrate the protein solution to at least 50 μM with a centrifugal filter device.
Verify the concentration by measuring the UV absorbance at 280 nm.
Add reducing agent and incubate the protein at room temperature for 1 hr.
Remove DTT from the solution by buffer exchange if used.
Add 3-10 mole equivalents of the fluorophore dropwise to the protein solution.
Ensure homogeneous mixing by gentle pipetting.
Incubate the mixture 1 hr at 37°C, 2 hr at room temperature, or overnight at 4°C.
Remove excess fluorophore by buffer exchange using centrifugal filters or dialysis.
Wash sufficiently so that no trace dye is detectable by UV absorbance of the flowthrough.
Add 1 mole equivalent (or substoichiometric amounts) of donor fluorophore dropwise to the protein solution.
Ensure homogeneous mixing by gentle pipetting.
Incubate for 1 hr at 37°C, 2 hr at room temperature, or overnight at 4°C.
Alternatively, add 5 mole equivalents of acceptor fluorophore and purify the donor-acceptor pair from other permutations present in the sample by HPLC or high-resolution ion-exchange chromatography.
If only donor was added above, separate from free dye as in step 7a.
Reduce the protein again if step 4b is performed overnight.
Remove reducing agent (DTT) before adding acceptor fluorophore.
Alternatively, single-labeled protein can be separated from unlabeled protein at this step by HPLC or a high-resolution ion exchange chromatography.
Measure the concentration of the donor-only single-labeled protein.
Add a 5× molar excess of acceptor fluorophore.
Incubate for 1 hour at 37°C, 2 hours at room temperature, or overnight at 4°C.
Perform step 7a again.
Verify purity and identity of the labeled proteins.
Measure the labeling percentage by UV-Vis spectroscopy using the provided formula.
If needed, further purify the labeled proteins by HPLC or high-resolution ion-exchange chromatography.
Verify the correct mass by LC-MS (or other MS method).
Aliquot the labeled protein.
Snap-freeze the aliquoted protein in liquid nitrogen or a dry ice/ethanol bath.
Fill each surface or well with 10% Tween 20 and incubate it for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Discard the Tween 20 solution from the chamber using a vacuum suction system.
Avoid contaminating the objective facing side of the glass surface with Tween 20.
Wash the chamber thoroughly with Milli-Q-filtered water.
Dry the chambers under light vacuum.
Store the dried chambers up to 1 month at room temperature.
Sandwich a spacer of double-sided tape or Parafilm between two coverslips or a glass slide and a coverslip to prepare the chamber.
Replace the quartz slide with borosilicate glass in the sandwich system to reduce cost for detecting freely diffusing molecules.
Place an appropriate concentration of donor-only labeled sample into the sample chamber.
Record raw photon counts in both donor and acceptor channels.
Subtract the average number of photons for buffer-only sample to perform background correction.
Place an equimolar mixture of donor and acceptor fluorophore in the sample chamber.
Excite with a laser suitable for donor fluorophore excitation.
Ensure all optical filters for the acceptor are in place.
